subject: Joint Resolution to Make Medford Hunger-Free
overview: The Council joined the Mayor and School Committee in a resolution pledging to eliminate food insecurity in the city by 2028. Members also approved pilot programs for new road and sidewalk maintenance techniques and reviewed the status of the regional Eversource transmission line project.

items.title: Joint resolution to make Medford hunger-free
items.summary: Approved a resolution setting a goal for Medford to be hunger-free by January 1, 2028, following testimony from the Greater Boston Food Bank and Project Bread regarding local food insecurity data.

items.title: Common victualler licenses
items.summary: Approved licenses for 400 Cafe and Lives Juice and Akai Bar.

items.title: Eversource project update
items.summary: Received a construction update on the 115kV underground transmission line and requested a legal opinion on whether the utility is required to upgrade aging city-owned pipes encountered during excavation.

items.title: Recognition of Justin Springer
items.summary: Approved a resolution honoring Medford native Justin Springer as a 2019 ABCD Community Hero.

items.title: Auburn Street guardrail replacement
items.summary: Requested that the DCR replace a damaged guardrail near Whole Foods to protect pedestrians.

items.title: PILOT commission draft ordinance
items.summary: Referred a report from the city solicitor regarding a Payment In Lieu Of Taxes (PILOT) commission to the Committee of the Whole.

items.title: Pilot program for recycled asphalt
items.summary: Approved a pilot program to resurface streets using recycled asphalt and requested that the state increase Chapter 90 funding.

items.title: Pilot program for sidewalk repair
items.summary: Approved a pilot program to use saw-cutting to eliminate sidewalk trip hazards instead of full panel replacement, pending discussion with collective bargaining units.

items.title: Presidential primary call
items.summary: Approved the official call and polling locations for the March 3, 2020, presidential preferential primary.

items.title: Condolences and meeting dedication
items.summary: Dedicated the meeting to the memory of John Byers and offered condolences to his family.

items.title: South and Main Street safety concerns
items.summary: Discussed ongoing safety issues and a potential $5 million state bond bill for traffic improvements following a recent pedestrian accident; the Council voted to forward previous safety recommendations to the new administration.

items.title: Medford Community Media recognition
items.summary: Recognized the local access station for its nomination for a Mass Creator Award for its mayoral debate coverage.
